description: Curated Studio collaboration episodes with source-read Issue-to-PR relationships and complete selected PR branch-commit membership.

methodology.source_basis: The earlier dated collaboration extract supplied episode candidates. This bounded follow-up reads current public Issue and PR bodies and complete commit membership for eight selected merged PRs; the earlier snapshot files remain unchanged.
methodology.population: Eight editorial episodes selected for materially different collaboration methods: adaptation, native state, measurement, promotion, specimen preservation, compact reception, financial adoption and local interaction repair.
methodology.issue_measure: Count distinct Issues directly addressed within the selected PR scope. A first tranche can address an umbrella Issue without completing all of it. Context, strategy recipients and successor Issues remain separately classified and excluded from the episode Issue count.
methodology.commit_measure: Count distinct SHA-identified commit objects listed by GitHub for the selected PR branches. The all-member measure includes merge commits; the companion nonmerge measure excludes records with more than one parent. Each episode deduplicates its selected PR members.
methodology.receiving_commit_measure: The PR's merge_commit_sha identifies the accepted receiving event separately. A PR member count is branch history, not the count of new receiving-branch commits or unique patches. Squash, merge and promotion conventions keep their own meanings.
methodology.relation_method: Read each selected PR body and corresponding Issue scope. Retain a short paraphrased warrant and public sources for every edge. Explicit implementation, first-tranche, research resolution and primary-route completion relations count; information, prepared successors and held work remain context.
methodology.missingness: An unselected or unclassified relation remains outside this bounded graph. A missing edge means no claim in this selection, rather than zero work or the absence of a relationship.
methodology.overlap: An Issue may occur in several episodes. A commit may be shared by several PR branches, especially a promotion. Within-episode counts remain useful; global counts use unions rather than summed episode memberships.
methodology.interpretation: These records describe scope and delivery history. They leave working hours, causal contribution shares, productivity, AI performance and the final future showcase endpoint unspecified.
methodology.public_boundary: Only public repository URLs, public record identities, commit SHAs and normalized source-grounded summaries are retained. Raw bodies, query-bearing retrieval URLs, gated locators and machine paths remain outside this extract.
